dedupe_keys.name: electrical distribution grid maps modelled medium voltage grid for six african countries meta ai for good hdx

description: Electrical Distribution Grid Maps is a Humanitarian Data Exchange dataset from AI for Good at Meta, then Facebook, giving model-predicted locations of medium-voltage distribution lines, which link high-voltage transmission to low-voltage supply. The page says the model combines public datasets such as night-time satellite imagery, roads and political boundaries: monthly VIIRS images are composited and filtered to remove background and reflected light before lines are inferred. Outputs are provided for Malawi, Nigeria, Uganda, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cote d'Ivoire and Zambia as CSV files and zipped GeoTIFF rasters at Bing tile level 20, and the model code and documentation are public on GitHub. The data are free to download under CC BY and date from early 2019, when the page was last modified. Coverage is these six countries. Caveats: accuracy is about 70 percent against ground-truthed data, and the page says the project is no longer active and has been carried on by others, mostly at the World Bank, through gridfinder. Simulation uses are an estimated distribution network where no utility map exists, for exposure and access studies. Related records: model-gridfinder is the successor method for global grid estimates.
